title: Bounded-size subobject surjecting onto a quotient
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with generator $U$. For an object $M$, let $|M|$ be the cardinality of its set of subobjects [lem-pur-kinjective-set-iso-classes-bounded-size]. Define $c(\lambda)=|\bigoplus_{\lambda}U|$. For every surjection $\pi:M\twoheadrightarrow N$ there exists a subobject $M'\subset M$ such that $M'\twoheadrightarrow N$ and $|M'|\le c(|N|)$.

proof.text: For every proper subobject N' of N, the inverse image pi^{-1}(N') is a proper subobject of M, since otherwise N' would contain pi(M)=N. The generator property therefore gives a morphism phi_{N'}:U\to M that does not factor through pi^{-1}(N'). Consequently pi\circ phi_{N'}:U\to N does not factor through N'.

Let P=\bigoplus_{N'}U be the coproduct of the maps phi_{N'} indexed by all proper subobjects N' of N, and let M' be its image in M. The index set is a subset of the set of subobjects of N, so it has cardinality at most |N|. Since M' is a quotient of P, sending a subobject of M' to its inverse image in P injects the subobject set of M' into the subobject set of P. The coproduct P is a direct summand, hence a subobject, of the coproduct of |N| copies of U (after enlarging the index set), so |M'| is at most |\bigoplus_{|N|}U|=c(|N|).

source.place: Lemma lemma-surjection-bounded-size, proof, displayed definition of M'

proof.text: The image M' surjects onto N: if its image were contained in a proper subobject N' of N, then the composite pi\circ phi_{N'} for the summand indexed by N' would factor through N', contradicting Step 1. Therefore M' is the required subobject, with |M'| \le c(|N|).

Step 2 treats M' as a quotient (image) of the coproduct and bounds its subobjects via inverse images in the coproduct, which embeds as a direct summand in the larger coproduct. Step 3 then proves surjectivity by the selected summand contradiction. No child node was needed.
